native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies significantly based on habitat type: it is highest in coastal areas, wetlands, urban environments, and riparian habitats (where gardening non-natives occur in 36% to 50% of plots, with mean richness of 0.57 to 0.79 species per plot), intermediate in croplands (20.7% of plots, mean richness of 0.22 species per plot), and lowest or absent in meadows, coniferous forests, broad-leaved forests, scrublands, and rock outcrops (0% to 7.7% of plots, mean richness <= 0.10 species per plot).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots across 10 habitats); calculated descriptive statistics for n.gard (mean, std, median, presence rate, proportion of total invaders); conducted omnibus Kruskal-Wallis and Chi-square contingency tests; computed all pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction; fitted Poisson GLMs with HC0 robust standard errors controlling for elevation and urban cover; synthesized empirical findings into a structured natural-language hypothesis.

sub_hypo.text: The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies significantly by habitat: it is highest in coastal areas, wetlands, urban environments, and riparian habitats (36%–50% of plots; mean richness 0.57–0.79 species per plot), intermediate in croplands (20.7% of plots; mean richness 0.22 species per plot), and lowest or absent in meadows, coniferous forests, broad-leaved forests, scrublands, and rock outcrops (0%–7.7% of plots; mean richness ≤0.10 species per plot).
sub_hypo.context: Gardening-introduced non-native plants in 632 plots across the ten studied habitat types in Barcelona province.
